javax.microedition.broadcast.recording
Class RecordingScheduler

java.lang.Object
  javax.microedition.broadcast.recording.RecordingScheduler

public class RecordingScheduler
extends java.lang.Object

The scheduler for scheduling and managing recordings. This class can be used to schedule recordings that can happen outside the life cycle of the Java application or MIDlet; i.e. a previously scheduled recording can take place even when the MIDlet or the VM is not running. If the implementation doesn't support this kind of behavior, the constructor of Recording throws UnsupportedOperationException exception.

Default Components Selection

When a selected service contains multiple alternatives for a given kind of ServiceComponents, the RecordingScheduler implementation will choose one default component based on the preference set in the receiver using setPreference(String,Object). For example, a service may contain more than one audio tracks, each of which is recorded in a different language. In that case, only one of these audio tracks is recorded. The selection of default components is basically implementation-specific. It may differ from one broadcast technology to another, from one broadcaster to another, or from one receiver to another. Therefore JSR 272 does not define a standard policy for it.

But every implementation of RecordingScheduler must respect at least, one standard preference, LANGUAGE. In addition to that, implementation-specific preferences may be defined and respected by some implementations. In evaluating preferences set to a RecordingScheduler against components contained in a service, there may be occasions where no components are fully compliant with the current preferences. For example, the system preference may be set to a particular language. But that language may not be available at all in a service. In that case, the RecordingScheduler implementation must still record at least one available component rather than picking nothing.

Preference Setting

Preferences can be set to a RecordingScheduler to affect its behavior. For example, LANGUAGE preference may be set to affect the choice of the default components based on the language associated with each component. The LANGUAGE preference is mandatory, and every implementation should respect it when selecting default components from a service. Note that implementations may add additional preferences and respect them. The list of all the recognized preference keys can be obtained via getAllPreferenceKeys().

Field Detail

LANGUAGE

public static final java.lang.String LANGUAGE
The preferred language of choice. This is mandatory, so every RecordingScheduler implementation must respect the setting of this preference. It may affect the selection of, for example, the default audio track when more than one audio tracks are available in various languages. The value shall be a language tag defined in RFC 3066.

See Also:

add

public static void add(Recording recording)
                throws BroadcastServiceException
Adds the given recording to the scheduled recordings list. RecordingSchedulerListener.listUpdated() is called before this method returns.

Parameters:
recording - The program to record.
Throws:
UnsupportedOperationException - Thrown if the scheduled recording is not supported by the implementation at all
java.lang.NullPointerException - if the given recording is null
java.lang.SecurityException - if the user did not have rights to do the operation
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - Thrown if program has ended already or if it doesn't exist.
BroadcastServiceException - Thrown if the given recording overlaps in time with a recording already in the recordings list and the implementation does not support recording multiple recordings at the same time.

The value will be non-empty even in the beginning of the lifecycle of the application, since the implementation might remember the storage location from the previous runs of the application or native applications can also affect this value.

java.lang.SecurityException - if user has no rights to get the recording directory

listRecordings

public static Recording[] listRecordings()
Lists all the recordings. The list of recordings represents all the recordings which are not in Recording.STATE_UNDETERMINED state. To determine the state of indvidual recordings, use Recording.getState(). If no recording can be found, a zero-length array will be returned.

The list of recording is persistent across the execution lifecycle of the applications. Therefore, when an application starts, there may already be existing recordings from the previous execution sessions. In addition, the list of recordings may also be affected by any native components managing the recordings list outside the lifecycle of the running Java application. RecordingSchedulerListener may be used to listen for any changes to the list of recordings.

Returns:
The list of recordings which are not in Recording.STATE_UNDETERMINED state.
Throws:
UnsupportedOperationException - thrown if the scheduled recording is not supported by the implementation at all
java.lang.SecurityException - if user has no rights to list recordings

remove

public static void remove(Recording recording)
Removes the given recording from the recording list. If the recording has already taken place (or is currently recording), the file will be deleted from the system. listRecordings() can be used to get an instance of the Recording for removal. RecordingSchedulerListener.listUpdated() is called before this method returns.

Parameters:
recording - The recording to remove.
Throws:
UnsupportedOperationException - Thrown if the scheduled recording is not supported by the implementation at all
java.lang.NullPointerException - if the given recording is null
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - Thrown if the given recording does not exist in the recording list.
java.lang.SecurityException - Thrown if the user did not have rights to remove the given Recording.
